newsitem.title: JAPAN: Peru will not charge Japanese reporter over entry.
newsitem.headline: Peru will not charge Japanese reporter over entry.

text.p: Peru has decided not to press charges against a Japanese television reporter and his interpreter for entering the Lima compound where 72 hostages are being held by a rebel group, the network said on Sunday.

The Peruvian authorities had been considering charges of terrorism and treason against Tsuyoshi Hitomi, 27, a New York-based reporter for Asahi Television, and his interpreter after they entered the Japanese ambassador's residence without permission.
"The Peruvian authorities were investigating Hitomi and his interpreter on suspicion of terrorist activities but they have decided that there is no evidence of such activities," the spokesman said.
"There will be no further legal action from the Peruvian government," he said.
The two entered the residence on January 7 after eluding a police cordon by passing through two private homes neighbouring the ambassador's complex that had been rented by the network.
Once inside, Hitomi interviewed the leader of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, Nestor Cerpa Cartolini.
The two were detained by Peruvian police for four days. Hitomi has since returned to New York.
TV Asahi President Kunio Ito said on Wednesday that Hitomi's action was "rash" and that "the whole affair lacked discretion".
TV Asahi has not broadcast the footage shot inside the embassy but has not decided whether to do so in the future, the spokesman said.
